Video footage released by the Department of Homeland Security showed a man holding a baby notice something wrong with the child and begin ...
inputs.modified_text:
Let’s be entirely clear about what is really going on here. The state is running a transparent propaganda machine, desperately trying to force us to applaud the repressive machinery of the state simply because an individual agent performed a basic human function. They are trying to redeem an institution built on cruelty, family separation, and the systemic terrorization of marginalized communities. 

Just look at the feel-good narratives and video footage handed down by the Department of Homeland Security, centering on an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent springing into action on Thursday at JFK International Airport in New York. A family was subjected to the indignities, stress, and structural violence of a crowded TSA line—a direct product of a security apparatus that subjects vulnerable people, including infants, to dehumanizing conditions. 

Instead of examining the systemic failures that put working-class families and immigrants into these frantic, unsafe environments, the state apparatus wants us to focus on a singular, dramatic moment involving a baby stuck in a crowded TSA line with his family stopped breathing at an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent jumped into action. 

It is a transparent attempt to humanize an inherently inhumane agency. No amount of selective storytelling about Thursday at JFK International Airport in New York can wash away the systemic violence of ICE or the oppressive realities of these heavily policed transit hubs. We need institutional abolition and true structural reform, not propaganda meant to distract us from the daily suffering inflicted by border enforcement and security theater.
